function: Learned (DDQN) allocation of frame time slots among K UAVs relaying to a serving LEO satellite, minimizing the maximum queue length, i.e. latency (p. 6, p. 11).
system: K=4 UAVs relay ground users to LEO satellites (L=5, 10, 25), 100 MHz bandwidth, 25 dBm, shadowed-Rician erasure link; antennas and carrier band not stated; no RIS (p. 4).
method: Double DQN with four hidden layers of 512 neurons; reinforcement learning trained offline on a cloud server for 200 episodes, then deployed on the LEO satellite (p. 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: erasure channel with shadowed-Rician fading, orbits from Skyfield library using Starlink data, Poisson packet arrivals; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurement (p. 4, p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained with K=4, C=15 slots, arrival rates {2,2,2,5} (p. 12); tested on queue trajectories over 400 frames and arrival-rate sweeps with L=5, 10, 25 (p. 12-13); no stated shift.
baselines: DDQN has no baseline; the convex min-max approach is compared only with the non-learned longest-queue scheduler of reference [14] (p. 10).
metrics: Maximum and average queue length, QoS exponent, accumulated reward, total allocated slots, FLOPs (p. 10-13).
complexity: Inference FLOPs of the DDQN as a function of action-space size, formula (58) checked against THOP counts in Fig. 10 (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "shadowed-Rician fading can be considered". The channel is a custom erasure-channel simulator (Table I, path-loss exponent 3); Starlink-based orbits from Skyfield only drive the UAV-LEO distance; no 3GPP TR 38.811 model or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "Varying Average Arrival Rates" (Fig. 12 on p. 13, L = 5, 10, 25) is a sweep; the paper never states that the DDQN trained on the Table III setting was tested in a new scenario or adapted.
q3_support: p. 10: "compared to the baseline approach in (55)". The only baseline is a non-learned longest-queue scheduler [14], used against the convex min-max approach; the DDQN results (pp. 12-13) have no non-learned baseline and no earlier learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 12: "theoretically calculated FLOPs" based on (58) for the DDQN inference, compared with THOP counts in Fig. 10.
q5_support: p. 11: "executed using PyTorch". No code or data link is given for the paper itself; only third-party tools (CVX, THOP) are cited, and the channel is simulated.
notes: Included as area 6: DDQN slot allocation for UAV-to-LEO links (p. 6, p. 11). Borderline above_phy: the allocation uses queue states and resembles scheduling, but the instructions treat learned resource allocation on satellite and aerial links as physical layer; reviewer to confirm. The convex min-max approach (p. 5-6) is non-learned. Title and DOI on p. 1 match the DOI listed.
